texts.facts: During investigation, statement of injured Mohd. Sagir was recorded who stated that on 24.05.2023, he was carrying bolt of cloth on his scooty. When he reached Modi Mill flyover and was waiting at the red light, at about 04:45 PM, the offending vehicle forcefully hit the vehicles waiting behind the petitioner. As a result, the Wagon R car struck against the scooty of the petitioner due to which petitioner got hit and fell. Petitioner was taken to Fortis hospital where he received treatment and was later referred to AIIMS Trauma Center where he remained admitted till 29.05.2023. 3. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while the present DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3/United India Insurance Company is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. In reply to the DAR filed by driver/respondent No. 1, the occurrence of the accident or the fact of offending vehicle being driven by respondent No. 1 has not been denied though the allegations of rash and negligent driving have been denied. To prove his claim, petitioner Mohd. Sagir led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He testifies on the lines of the DAR and deposed that on 24.05.2023 at about 04:40 p.m., he was riding his scooty bearing No. DL-3SET-2369 and was returning to his house from Lajpat Nagar with some cloth on his scooty. When he reached the red light at Masigar and was waiting for the traffic signal to turn green, all of the sudden, a bus bearing No. DL-1PD-0202, being driven in rash and negligent manner and at a high speed by its driver Neeraj Kumar, came from Modi Mill flyover side and hit a taxi which was just behind the scooty of the petitioner. The said taxi ran over and crushed petitioner's left leg. The offending bus also hit other vehicles which were at the traffic signal. PW-1 further deposed that he was taken to Fortis hospital where he received primary treatment for amputated leg and referred PW-1 to AIIMS Trauma Center. PW-1 remained admitted from 24.05.2023 to 29.05.2023 during which he was operated. He deposed that he was under observation of the doctors till date. He was also unable to carry out his daily routine independently. PW-1 deposed that he had spent more than Rs. 5 lakhs on his treatment, special diet, conveyance, expenses etc. and that he is required to get prosthetic limb implanted. He deposed that he had suffered permanent disability, loss of income, pain and mental agony etc. for which he claimed Rs. 75 lakhs as compensation. Final arguments in detail were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income as Rs.1,03,404/-. life expectancy of 70 years, he was awarded as sum of Rs.7,80,000/- towards cost of prosthetic limb assuming replacement of limb every 5 to 6 years. The petitioner shall thereafter meet the AGM of insurance company who shall personally monitor that the artificial limb has been installed and confirm the same to the SBI Bank where the Award amount would be deposited by the insurance company. texts.arguments: . Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. He has categorically stated that the accident occurred due to negligence of the offending vehicle as its struck the vehicles behind the vehicle of the petitioner. The averment has not been refuted by the driver of the offending bus specifically in the reply. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him.
